info.name: paccradle API: sign-in (2026-10-29)
info.description:
Change: M1-D3, sign-in (2026-10-29). Client and admin contracts move to **1.0.0-beta.2** (`api-version`). Merge into the main contract.

**Sessions.** Every sign-in and refresh answers with a session body and sets the refresh cookie (`HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Secure` on HTTPS; `Path=/api/{surface}/v1/auth`). The web app keeps the access token in memory and sends `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`; fetch with `credentials: 'include'` so the cookie travels. Access tokens last 15 minutes on the client (5 on the back office). Session responses are `no-store` and never compressed.

**Accounts.** A visitor is a guest until they confirm an email with a link. The link signs them in; the web app then asks for a password (`next_steps: set_password`) and offers a passkey on devices that support one (`add_passkey`). Later sign-ins: passkey first; after 2 failed passkey tries, password; forgot password = ask for an email link, sign in, set a new password within 15 minutes.

**Origin check.** Every `/auth` route refuses an `Origin` header other than the surface's web origin (`FORBIDDEN`). Sign-in routes share a per-address limit (`RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_PER_MINUTE`, default 20); refresh and sign-out keep the API-wide one.

**New error codes:** `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS` (401), `AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED` (401), `AUTH_LINK_INVALID` (400), `AUTH_ACCOUNT_REQUIRED` (403), `AUTH_REAUTH_REQUIRED` (403, `meta.fresh_minutes`), `AUTH_PASSWORD_REJECTED` (400, `meta.min_length`, `meta.max_length`), `AUTH_PASSKEY_REJECTED` (400), `AUTH_PASSKEY_ALREADY_REGISTERED` (409). The web app's fetch hook refreshes only on `AUTH_REQUIRED`.

**Passkey JSON.** `public_key` and `credential` use the W3C WebAuthn JSON shapes (camelCase, base64url), unlike the rest of the API: pass them straight to and from the browser.

request.description: A visitor who hasn't signed up gets a guest account at once, so they can capture and design. Call it on the first action that needs a user, if `/auth/refresh` found no session. Answers 201 with a session; the refresh token is in the `paccradle_refresh` cookie (HttpOnly; send requests with `credentials: 'include'`). A guest's captures, products and designs move to their account when they sign up or sign in from this browser.

item.name: Ask for an email link (sign up or sign in)

request.description: One endpoint for **sign up**, **email me a link** and **forgot password**. An address with no account gets "Confirm your email" (the link makes the account; valid 24 hours); an address with one gets a sign-in link (valid 15 minutes). The answer is 202 with no body either way, so nobody learns whether an address has an account. The link is `{APP_WEB_URL}/auth/link#token=…`: the web app reads the token from the fragment and calls *Sign in with an email link*. Each new link for an address is sent, but once one is used the others stop working. At most 3 per address per 10 minutes.

item.name: Sign in with an email link

request.description: Uses the token from the link (once). Confirms the address; makes the account if there is none (the browser's guest becomes it, keeping its work); otherwise signs in to it (a guest's work moves over). Send the guest's cookie if there is one. `next_steps` tells the web app what to offer: `set_password` when the account has none, `add_passkey` after any sign-in that didn't use a passkey (offer it only where `PublicKeyCredential.isUserVerifyingPlatformAuthenticatorAvailable()` is true).

request.description: Email (any letter case) and password. Every mismatch (no account, no password set, wrong password) is the same 401 and takes the same time. At most 5 tries per address per minute, on top of the per-address-IP sign-in limit. The web app's fallback order: passkey first; after 2 failed passkey tries, the password form and "Email me a sign-in link" (forgot password).

request.description: Swaps the refresh cookie for a new access token and a new cookie (the session lasts 30 days from the last refresh). Call it on start-up and when a request answers `AUTH_REQUIRED`. A cookie that was already swapped within 30 s (two tabs racing) gets an access token and no new cookie; one swapped longer ago ends the session (it may have been stolen). `AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED` clears the cookie: show sign-in.
